hints: Focus on what you actually have, impure ore, not pure MnO2. How many kg of MnO2 are in 1 tonne of this ore?
Now find what fraction of MnO2 is manganese by using Ar values, Mn = 54.9 and O = 16.0 to get Mr of MnO2.
Multiply the mass of MnO2 you found by the Mn fraction to get the mass of Mn alone, and check your units in kg.
walkthrough:
**Find the mass of MnO2 in the ore**

Remember 1 tonne = 1000 kg. The ore is only 4% MnO2 by mass.

$$\text{mass of MnO}_2 = \frac{4}{100} \times 1000 \text{ kg} = 40.0 \text{ kg}$$

**Find the fraction of Mn in MnO2**

Only part of MnO2 is manganese, the rest is oxygen. Use relative masses.

$$M_r(\text{MnO}_2) = 54.9 + (2 \times 16.0) = 86.9$$
$$\text{fraction of Mn} = \frac{54.9}{86.9} = 0.632$$

**Convert MnO2 mass to Mn mass**

Multiply the 40.0 kg of MnO2 by the Mn fraction. This is the key idea, mass of element = mass of compound x mass fraction.

$$\text{mass of Mn} = 40.0 \text{ kg} \times 0.632 = 25.3 \text{ kg}$$

options.A: Correct. 40.0 kg of MnO2 contains 40.0 x (54.9/86.9) = 25.3 kg of Mn. This correctly applies both the 4% purity and the molar mass fraction.
options.B: Incorrect. 40.0 kg is the mass of MnO2 in 1 tonne of ore, not the mass of Mn. This trap forgets that oxygen also contributes to the mass of MnO2, so you must multiply by 54.9/86.9.
options.C: Incorrect. 63.3 kg is approximately the mass of Mn in 100 kg of pure MnO2. This trap calculates the percentage composition correctly (63.2%) but forgets to first find the 40 kg of MnO2 present in the 1 tonne of 4% ore.
options.D: Incorrect. 632 kg is approximately the mass of Mn in 1 tonne of pure MnO2. This trap forgets the ore is only 4% MnO2 and so is about 25 times too large.
